---
title: "Session 1: Introduction to R for Actuaries"
---

## Theme

From raw actuarial data to a clean dataset.

This session teaches the first part of the mini-project workflow: importing policy and claims data, inspecting structure, and performing basic validation checks.

## Learning Outcomes

At the end of this session, participants will be able to:

- Navigate the RStudio environment and organise an R Project.
- Import actuarial datasets into R.
- Understand the main R data structures used in actuarial analysis.
- Manipulate and validate policy and claims data using `dplyr`.
- Perform common data quality checks, including missing values, duplicates, data types, and consistency checks.
- Produce the first reproducible Quarto notebook for the case study.

## Case Study Milestone

Participants reproduce Sections 1 and 2 of the mini-project:

- Read `data/raw/policies.csv`.
- Read `data/raw/claims.csv`.
- Convert date columns.
- Check row counts, missing values, duplicates, policy IDs, claim dates, and numeric ranges.
- Document what they found.

## Suggested Timing

| Time | Activity |
|---:|---|
| 15 min | RStudio, projects, files, and Quarto orientation |
| 25 min | Importing policies and claims data |
| 35 min | Data structures and `dplyr` basics |
| 25 min | Data quality checks from the mini-project |
| 15 min | AI checkpoint and reflection |
| 5 min | Wrap-up |

## Core Code From The Mini-Project

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Load packages.
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the raw files.
policies <- read_csv("data/raw/policies.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
claims <- read_csv("data/raw/claims.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Convert text dates into real Date objects.
policies <- policies |>
  mutate(policy_start = as.Date(policy_start))

claims <- claims |>
  mutate(claim_date = as.Date(claim_date))

# Inspect the data.
glimpse(policies)
glimpse(claims)

# Find claims that do not match a known policy.
unmatched_claims <- claims |>
  anti_join(policies, by = "policy_id")
```

## AI Checkpoint

1. Attempt the validation check independently.
2. Ask AI to explain one unfamiliar line of code.
3. Ask AI what assumptions the check makes.
4. Run the code yourself and inspect the output.
5. Rewrite the result in your own words.
